cues: One thing most notes leave out.
De Burgos wrote in Spanish; you read Jack Agüeros's English translation.
Images, structure and argument survive translation, so discuss them with confidence.
But sound and rhythm belong to the translator, so never say the poet uses alliteration without adding, in the English version.
And something is lost: Spanish adjectives mark the speaker as a woman in every line; English cannot.
The free verse shape, though, is hers.
One sentence in the exam is enough.
